sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *aunque* (“although, even though”) from A2 Unit 28. With a fact that is true, the verb after *aunque* is in the indicative. It is the natural word for the main puzzle of the 1990s: the economy grew, but inequality did not fall.

items.spanish: Aunque la economía creció, la desigualdad no bajó.
items.english: Although the economy grew, inequality did not fall.

items.spanish: Aunque había más trabajo, muchos empleos eran informales.
items.english: Although there was more work, many jobs were informal.

items.spanish: Aunque algunos sectores ganaron mucho dinero, muchas familias no vieron esa riqueza.
items.english: Although some sectors earned a lot of money, many families did not see that wealth.

items.spanish: El descontento crecía, aunque las reformas seguían.
items.english: Discontent was growing, even though the reforms continued.

sections.content: The *aunque* clause can come first (with a comma) or second. Do not add *pero* in the same sentence: *Aunque creció, la desigualdad no bajó*, not *Aunque creció, pero …*.
